full_text_en:
**Gudongchun Co., Ltd. v. Yiqingyuan Co., Ltd. et al. — Dispute over Unfair Competition**

**Ruling Summary**

Article 97 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Citizens shall enjoy the right of discovery with respect to their discoveries. Persons who have made discoveries shall have the right to apply for and obtain certificates of discovery, bonuses or other awards." According to this provision, the right of discovery is only a right to honor and a right to be awarded that is granted to an individual or a collective making the discovery, and it cannot be assigned or acquired by succession.

Article 3 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants provides: "The administrative departments of agriculture and forestry under the State Council (hereinafter collectively referred to as the examination and approval authorities) shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, be jointly responsible for the acceptance and examination of applications for the protection of new varieties of plants, and shall grant new variety rights (hereinafter referred to as variety rights) for new plant varieties that comply with the provisions of these Regulations." Article 31 of the same Regulations provides: "For an application for a new variety that, after substantive examination, complies with the provisions of these Regulations, the examination and approval authority shall make a decision to grant the variety right, issue a certificate of variety right, and register and announce the same." According to the above provisions, the acquisition of a new plant variety right must be carried out in accordance with statutory procedures; without statutory procedures, no individual or entity may originally acquire a variety right in any other manner.

**Plaintiff:** Hunan Taoyuan County Gudongchun Tea Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at Taipingpu Village, Taipingpu Township, Taoyuan County.

**Legal Representative:** Lu Wanjun, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Hunan Yiqingyuan Tea Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at Fengquan Building, Caie South Road, Changsha City.

**Legal Representative:** Jian Bohua, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Zhang Guohua, male, Han nationality, 54 years old, proprietor of Guangyuan Tea House, Wuling District, Changde City, residing at the middle section of Dongting Avenue, Changde City.

**Defendant:** Zhang Zhi, male, Han nationality, 27 years old, proprietor of Yiqingyuan Tea House, Wuling District, Changde City, residing at Dongjiang Village, Dongjiang Township, Changde City.

**Defendant:** Hunan Jiarunduo Supermarket Co., Ltd., Changde Store, domiciled at Renmin Middle Road, Changde City.

**Legal Representative:** Young David Colin, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Hunan Jiarunduo Supermarket Co., Ltd., Chenzhou Store, domiciled at Guoqing North Road, Chenzhou City.

**Legal Representative:** Young David Colin, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Hunan Jiarunduo Supermarket Co., Ltd., Chaoyang Store, domiciled at Renmin Road, Changsha City.

**Legal Representative:** Young David Colin, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Changsha Tongcheng Holding Co., Ltd., Dongtang Store, domiciled at Laodong West Road, Changsha City.

**Legal Representative:** Zhou Zhaoda, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Hunan Huayin Wanghe Supermarket Co., Ltd., Xinzhong Road Store, domiciled at Xinzhong Road Intersection, Shaoshan South Road, Changsha City.

**Legal Representative:** Zhang Yawu, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Hunan Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Supermarket Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dongfeng Road, Changsha City.

**Legal Representative:** Zhou Jie, General Manager.

**Defendant:** Hengyang Huayin Wanghe Supermarket Co., Ltd., Jiefang Road Store, domiciled at Jiefang Road, Hengyang City.

**Legal Representative:** Hu Ganjun, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Hunan Xinlianxin Supermarket Co., Ltd., Xiangtan Liangmao Store, domiciled at Chezhan Road, Xiangtan City.

**Legal Representative:** Huang Tengqi, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Hunan Taoyuan County Gudongchun Tea Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gudongchun Company), filed a lawsuit with the Changde Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province against the defendants Hunan Yiqingyuan Tea Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yiqingyuan Company), Zhang Guohua, Zhang Zhi, Hunan Jiarunduo Supermarket Co., Ltd., Changde Store (hereinafter referred to as Jiarunduo Changde Store), Hunan Jiarunduo Supermarket Co., Ltd., Chenzhou Store (hereinafter referred to as Jiarunduo Chenzhou Store), Hunan Jiarunduo Supermarket Co., Ltd., Chaoyang Store (hereinafter referred to as Jiarunduo Chaoyang Store), Changsha Tongcheng Holding Co., Ltd., Dongtang Store (hereinafter referred to as Tongcheng Holdings Dongtang Store), Hunan Huayin Wanghe Supermarket Co., Ltd., Xinzhong Road Store (hereinafter referred to as Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store), Hunan Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Supermarket Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company), Hengyang Huayin Wanghe Supermarket Co., Ltd., Jiefang Road Store (hereinafter referred to as Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store), and Hunan Xinlianxin Supermarket Co., Ltd., Xiangtan Liangmao Store (hereinafter referred to as Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store), on the ground of a dispute over unfair competition.

**Plaintiff's Allegations**

The "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plant was discovered by Lu Wanjun, the legal representative of Gudongchun Company. Through research and cultivation by Lu Wanjun and scientific research personnel, this variety was systematically bred and promoted, passed evaluation as a crop variety, and the research achievements have won multiple awards within Hunan Province. The "Ye Cha Wang" and "Ye Cha" series of products produced by Gudongchun Company using "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea as raw material have been sold nationwide and have gradually become a specialty product of Taoyuan, receiving favorable reviews from consumers. The defendant Yiqingyuan Company forged the place of origin on its product packaging, imitated Gudongchun Company's famous brand "Ye Cha Wang" and "Ye Cha" series, and made false publicity in the book *An Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* compiled by it as well as on its webpage, which constitutes unfair competition. Gudongchun Company requested a judgment ordering Yiqingyuan Company to cease the acts of unfair competition, make a public apology, and compensate for the economic losses of RMB 300,000 caused by its unfair competition, and ordering the other defendants to cease selling the series of infringing products of Yiqingyuan Company.

The plaintiff Gudongchun Company submitted the following evidence:

1. Photographs of the maternal parent tea plant of "Taoyuan Big Leaf" and the *Annals of Taoyuan County: Agricultural Annals*, to prove the fact that Lu Wanjun discovered, bred, and promoted the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea variety.
2. *Project Task Plan for the Three Science and Technology Projects*, *Selection and Breeding of New Varieties of Big Leaf Tea in Taoyuan County*, Science and Technology Achievement Appraisal Certificate No. (1989) Xiang Ke Jian Zi No. 127, evaluation materials for the tea plant variety, *Application for Evaluation of Crop Varieties of Hunan Province*, and award certificates, to prove that the right of discovery of the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea variety belonged to the predecessor of Gudongchun Company, Hunan Taoyuan County Tea Variety Station (hereinafter referred to as Taoyuan Tea Variety Station).
3. Packaging boxes for the Gudongchun brand "Ye Cha Wang" and "Ye Cha", to prove that Gudongchun Company had the right of prior use of the names "Ye Cha Wang" and "Ye Cha".
4. Product packaging boxes and sales invoices of the defendant Yiqingyuan Company, webpage materials and promotional advertisements of Yiqingyuan Company, and the book *An Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* compiled by Yiqingyuan Company, to prove the acts of unfair competition by Yiqingyuan Company and the fact that it does not have a "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plantation within Taoyuan County.
5. Relevant reports from *Xiaoxiang Morning Herald* and *Hunan Daily*, to prove the profits obtained by Yiqingyuan Company as a result of the unfair competition.
6. Business registration materials of Taoyuan Tea Variety Station and Gudongchun Company, to prove the succession relationship between the two and that Gudongchun Company is the proper subject for this lawsuit.
7. Invoices and packaging bags for the sale of "Ye Cha Wang", "Ye Cha Mao Jian", and "Ye Zhen Green Tea" by the defendants including Zhang Guohua, to prove the fact that Zhang Guohua et al. sold the infringing products of Yiqingyuan Company.

**Defendant Yiqingyuan Company's Defense**

The plaintiff Gudongchun Company does not have a right of discovery over "Taoyuan Big Leaf"; the "Ye Zhen Wang", "Ye Cha Mao Jian", "Ye Zhen Green Tea", and "Ye Zhen Mao Jian" produced by Yiqingyuan Company do not constitute infringement of Gudongchun Company's right to product names; Yiqingyuan Company did not forge the place of origin of "Taoyuan Big Leaf" and does not constitute unfair competition. Yiqingyuan Company requested that Gudongchun Company's claims be dismissed.

The defendant Yiqingyuan Company submitted the following evidence:

1. Document Xiang Nong Ye (1992) Zhong Zi No. 16, to prove that Taoyuan Tea Variety Station and the Tea Research Institute of Hunan Agricultural College (hereinafter referred to as the College Research Institute) were the discoverers of the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plant variety.
2. The *Shareholders' Agreement* of the plaintiff Gudongchun Company, to prove that there was no succession relationship between Gudongchun Company and Taoyuan Tea Variety Station.
3. An agreement dated August 10, 2001, to prove that Yiqingyuan Company had the right to use the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea brand.
4. Notifications of acceptance of trademark registration, to prove that Yiqingyuan Company had applied for trademark registration for "Ye Zhen Wang" and "Ye Jian Wang".

**Defendant Zhang Guohua's Defense**

Zhang Guohua stated that he had already ceased selling the tea products of the defendant Yiqingyuan Company, and requested that the plaintiff Gudongchun Company's claims against him be dismissed.

The defendant Zhang Guohua did not submit any evidence within the time limit for evidence submission.

**Defendants Jiarunduo Changde Store, Jiarunduo Chenzhou Store, Jiarunduo Chaoyang Store, Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store, Tongcheng Holdings Dongtang Store, Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company, Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store, and Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store's Defense**

These defendants stated that they only had a site lease relationship with the defendant Yiqingyuan Company, and the sales were organized by Yiqingyuan Company itself; therefore, they requested that the plaintiff Gudongchun Company's claims against them be dismissed.

The defendants Jiarunduo Changde Store, Jiarunduo Chenzhou Store, Jiarunduo Chaoyang Store, Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store, Tongcheng Holdings Dongtang Store, Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company, Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store, and Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store each submitted their *Exclusive Counter Use Agreement*, *Counter Lease Agreement*, etc., signed with the defendant Yiqingyuan Company, to support their defense.

**Defendant Zhang Zhi did not submit a defense.**

Upon trial, the Changde Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

In the autumn of 1969, Lu Wanjun, an employee of the Taipingpu Commune Tea Plantation in Taoyuan County, discovered a maternal wild tea plant of "Taoyuan Big Leaf" in the local area. Lu Wanjun and others conducted research under the guidance of former Associate Professor Zhu Xianming of Hunan Agricultural College, successfully carried out experiments on short-cuttage propagation of the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plant, and began systematic breeding and promotion. On December 12, 1989, the College Research Institute and Taoyuan Tea Variety Station jointly completed the scientific research project "Research on the Selection and Breeding of Improved Tea Plant Varieties Taoyuan No. 1 and No. 2," with principal researchers including Lu Wanjun, Tang Mingde, Li Juan, and Yuan Chunhua. The Hunan Provincial Science and Technology Commission appraised this scientific and technological achievement, determining that the variety had characteristics such as high yield, high quality, and strong stress resistance. In January 1992, the Hunan Provincial Crop Variety Evaluation Committee issued Certificate No. 107 (1) for Qualified Crop Varieties, evaluating and announcing that "Taoyuan Big Leaf" was a new tea plant variety selected and bred by Taoyuan Tea Variety Station and the College Research Institute. In May 1994, the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea of Taoyuan Tea Variety Station won the Science and Technology Innovation Gold Medal at the Hunan Provincial New Technology and New Products Trade Fair. In April 1995, it won a gold medal at the 1995 International Food and Processing Technology Expo.

The "Ye Cha Wang", "Ye Cha", and other series of products produced by Taoyuan Tea Variety Station and the plaintiff Gudongchun Company using "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea as raw material had won multiple awards since 1982 and gradually became a specialty product of Taoyuan, receiving favorable reviews from consumers. In November 1996, Taoyuan Tea Variety Station applied for cancellation of registration. The former staff of Taoyuan Tea Variety Station formed shareholders and established Gudongchun Company, which continued to engage in tea plant cultivation research. The original plant, equipment, and debts of Taoyuan Tea Variety Station were assumed by Gudongchun Company.

Since 1996, the defendant Yiqingyuan Company had indicated on the packaging bags of its products "Ye Zhen Mao Jian" and "Ye Zhen Green Tea" that "Yiqingyuan Ye Zhen Mao Jian is produced at the Hunan Yiqingyuan high-quality wild needle tea base in the Wuling Mountains, a region of layered peaks and year-round cloud and mist. The Ye Zhen Wang tea plant variety is an excellent variety derived from the wild big-leaf tea resources discovered in Taoyuan through systematic selection and breeding..." thereby engaging in advertising. The packaging bag of its product "Ye Cha Mao Jian" also stated that "this product uses Taoyuan wild tea big leaf as raw material." Yiqingyuan Company had also produced "Ye Cha Wang," which was the same product name as that of the plaintiff Gudongchun Company.

In the book *An Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* compiled by the defendant Yiqingyuan Company, "Taoyuan Big Leaf" was described as: "On April 5, 1976, a team led by Professor Zhu Xianming, a tea science expert from Hunan Agricultural University, while inspecting the ecological environment of tea plantations in the Wuling Mountains of Hunan, discovered a wild tea plant on a hillside in Lujiachong Village, Taipingpu Township, Taoyuan County, Changde, Hunan. ... Subsequently, the Hunan Provincial Department of Science and Technology organized experts to conduct variety identification and content analysis. Liu Gengling, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, and Long Xinping, Director of the Hunan Provincial Bureau of Township Enterprises, conducted special research on this wild tea variety. ... In December 1986, Professor Zhu Xianming, together with the Changde Municipal Bureau of Agriculture and Taoyuan County Tea Group, decided to name the variety 'Taoyuan Big Leaf'." "Ye Zhen Wang" was described as: "... selected and bred by the Yiqingyuan Company expert group from the wild 'Taoyuan Big Leaf' variety through asexual propagation, this variety is an excellent local large-leaf green tea variety in our country..." "Taoyuan Tea" was described as: "... this area is the main production area of the famous 'Taoyuan Big Leaf' variety and the Yiqingyuan Ye Zhen Wang variety..." Yiqingyuan Company also conducted the same publicity on its website.

The plaintiff Gudongchun Company purchased tea products "Ye Zhen Mao Jian", "Ye Cha Mao Jian", "Ye Zhen Green Tea", or "Ye Cha Wang" produced by the defendant Yiqingyuan Company from the tea houses operated by defendants Zhang Guohua and Zhang Zhi, as well as from defendants Jiarunduo Changde Store, Jiarunduo Chenzhou Store, Tongcheng Holdings Dongtang Store, Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store, Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company, Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store, and Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store, and obtained sales invoices from the above-mentioned sales units.

The Changde Intermediate People's Court held:

As confirmed by the relevant functional departments, "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea was a new tea plant variety discovered by Taoyuan Tea Variety Station, and the College Research Institute provided certain assistance in the breeding and promotion of the variety. Therefore, Taoyuan Tea Variety Station and the College Research Institute jointly enjoyed the right of discovery over the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea.

In November 1996, the plaintiff Gudongchun Company was established on the premise of accepting the assets and debts of Taoyuan Tea Variety Station. Therefore, there was a property succession relationship between Gudongchun Company and Taoyuan Tea Variety Station. Although the ownership of the variety right for "Taoyuan Big Leaf" was not explicitly clarified at the time of Gudongchun Company's establishment, Lu Wanjun, the discoverer of "Taoyuan Big Leaf", was the legal representative of Gudongchun Company. The relevant functional departments of Taoyuan County also recognized that the variety right for "Taoyuan Big Leaf" belonged to Gudongchun Company. Subsequently, the development and promotion of "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea were continuously carried out by Gudongchun Company. Therefore, Gudongchun Company effectively succeeded to the right of discovery of the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plant variety enjoyed by Taoyuan Tea Variety Station. The defendant Yiqingyuan Company did not have the right of discovery over "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea, nor did it acquire the right to use the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" variety through an agreement. Its false publicity caused consumers to mistakenly believe that the ingredient of Yiqingyuan Company's tea products was "Taoyuan Big Leaf" and that the place of origin of its tea raw materials was within Taoyuan County. Pursuant to Article 5, Paragraph (4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law), which prohibits "forging or fraudulently using certification marks, quality marks such as high-quality product marks, forging the place of origin, or making false representations that are misleading as to the quality of goods," and Article 9, Paragraph 1, which provides that "business operators shall not use advertising or other methods to make false or misleading representations as to the quality, ingredients, performance, use, producer, expiry date, place of origin, etc., of their goods," this act constituted an infringement of Gudongchun Company's right of discovery over the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plant variety.

The "Ye Cha Wang" and "Ye Cha" series products produced by the plaintiff Gudongchun Company using "Taoyuan Big Leaf" as raw material had achieved a certain degree of fame in China's tea market. Their product names had a certain narrative quality regarding the quality, raw materials, function, and use of the products and were not generic names for goods. Therefore, these products could be considered well-known goods. Pursuant to Article 5, Paragraph (2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, which prohibits "using without authorization the unique name, packaging, or decoration of a well-known good, or using a name, packaging, or decoration similar to those of another person's well-known good, thereby causing confusion with the well-known good of another person and leading purchasers to mistake it for that well-known good," and taking into account the industry practice in China's tea sector that "zhen" (needle) and "cha" (tea) have the same meaning, it could be found that "Ye Zhen Wang" produced by the defendant Yiqingyuan Company was similar to the name of Gudongchun Company's tea product, which could easily cause consumer confusion. Therefore, this constituted infringement of Gudongchun Company's unique name right for its "Ye Cha Wang" tea product.

The description of "Taoyuan Big Leaf" in *An Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* compiled by the defendant Yiqingyuan Company was inconsistent with the objective facts, which could easily lead others to mistakenly believe that Yiqingyuan Company had the right to use the new tea plant variety "Taoyuan Big Leaf". Therefore, Yiqingyuan Company had subjective fault. The book *An Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* compiled by Yiqingyuan Company denied the plaintiff Gudongchun Company's right of discovery over "Taoyuan Big Leaf", harming Gudongchun Company's interests. Additionally, Yiqingyuan Company used the compiled book to make false promotional advertisements for its tea products. According to Article 14 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, which provides that "business operators shall not fabricate or disseminate false facts to damage the business reputation or product reputation of a competitor," this act constituted unfair competition.

The plaintiff Gudongchun Company purchased "Ye Zhen Mao Jian", "Ye Cha Mao Jian", "Ye Zhen Green Tea", or "Ye Cha Wang" tea products produced by the defendant Yiqingyuan Company from the tea houses operated by defendants Zhang Guohua and Zhang Zhi, as well as from defendants Jiarunduo Changde Store, Jiarunduo Chenzhou Store, Tongcheng Holdings Dongtang Store, Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store, Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company, Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store, and Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store, and obtained sales invoices from the above-mentioned sales units. The fact that the above defendants sold the infringing products of Yiqingyuan Company was clear. Their defense that they only had site or counter lease agreements with Yiqingyuan Company and did not distribute Yiqingyuan Company's tea products was untenable.

The report in *Hunan Daily* on November 21, 2003, stated that the orders received by the defendant Yiqingyuan Company at the Fifth Agricultural Expo exceeded RMB 10 million. According to the characteristics of news reports, this should be true. Yiqingyuan Company's defense that it was only a news report and it did not actually obtain the reported profits was untenable. However, the plaintiff Gudongchun Company failed to provide evidence to prove the amount of profits obtained by Yiqingyuan Company from the production of infringing tea products such as "Ye Cha Wang" and "Ye Zhen Wang". Moreover, Yiqingyuan Company sold a series of tea products when participating in the Fifth Agricultural Expo. Therefore, in determining the specific amount of damages, the above factors, Yiqingyuan Company's sales costs, and other unpredictable market factors should be comprehensively considered. Hence, the RMB 300,000 in damages claimed by Gudongchun Company should be reduced, and an amount of RMB 100,000 was deemed appropriate.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), Articles 2, 5(2) and (4), 9(1), 14, and 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and Article 134(1)(1), (9), and (10) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of the Civil Law), the Changde Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on September 22, 2004:

1. The defendant Yiqingyuan Company shall immediately cease the acts of making false promotional advertisements using the "Taoyuan Big Leaf" tea plant variety on its tea product packaging bags and on relevant webpages of its website, and cease the advertising activities of making false representations regarding the place of origin of its tea products and the ingredients of its tea products;

2. The defendant Yiqingyuan Company shall, within five days after the effective date of this judgment, recall copies of the book *An Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* compiled by it according to its print run and destroy them;

3. The defendant Yiqingyuan Company shall, within five days after the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff Gudongchun Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 100,000;

**IV.** Defendant Yiqingyuan Company shall publish an apology statement approved by the court in *China Tea* magazine and on its internet website, and shall bear the relevant costs of publishing the apology statement;

**V.** Defendants Zhang Guohua, Zhang Zhi, Jiayongduo Changde Store, Jiayongduo Chenzhou Store, Jiayongduo Chaoyang Store, Tongcheng Kongtai Dongtang Store, Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store, Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company, Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store, and Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store shall cease selling the Yiqingyuan brand "Yezhenwang" and "Yechawang" tea products produced by Defendant Yiqingyuan Company, as well as the Yiqingyuan brand "Yezhen Maojian", "Yecha Maojian", and "Yezhen Green Tea" series of tea products whose packaging bags utilize "Taoyuan Daye" for false advertising.

Yiqingyuan Company, dissatisfied, appealed to the Hunan High People's Court. The grounds were: 1. The original judgment's findings on the "Taoyuan Daye" variety right were unclear, failing to ascertain the fact that the "Taoyuan Daye" variety right does not exist at all, and confusing the concepts of variety right with new plant varieties and the right to distribute agricultural products (including tea). 2. The finding that the appellant "forged the place of origin of the goods and made false representations as to the composition of the products" was erroneous. The "Entrusted Processing Agreement" and "Designated Production and Processing Agreement" entered into by the appellant and Taoyuan County Tengqiong Health Care Tea Factory are sufficient to prove that the raw materials for the Yezhenwang, Yezhen Maojian, and Yezhen Green Tea products produced and sold by the appellant originated within Taoyuan County. 3. There was insufficient evidence for the original judgment's finding that the appellant's "Yezhenwang" product infringed the appellee Gudongchun Company's exclusive name right of a well-known product, "Yechawang"; the appellee failed to prove that its "Yechawang" product was a well-known product or that "Yechawang" was its exclusive product name. 4. The original judgment erroneously applied the law; the cited provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law contained no provisions concerning the infringement of plant variety rights, and the legal basis for determining infringement of variety rights is the *Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of New Plant Varieties* (hereinafter the "Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties") and its Implementing Rules. The appellant requested the revocation of the original judgment and a new judgment according to law.

To support its grounds of appeal, Appellant Yiqingyuan Company submitted six additional sets of evidence.

**Set One:** The Notice of the Hunan Provincial Department of Agriculture on Publishing Crop Varieties That Passed Examination (Recognition) in January 1992 (hereinafter the "Notice"), used to prove: 1. "Taoyuan Daye" was examined and approved as a new tea tree variety by the Hunan Provincial Department of Agriculture on January 31, 1992; 2. The Notice states that "Taoyuan Daye" was a new variety selected and bred by the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station and the Research Institute of the Agricultural College, and Appellee Gudongchun Company is not listed in this Notice; 3. The Notice confirms the new variety and its origin, not a confirmation of variety right.

**Set Two:** Proof from Peng Xinde and the "Catalog of New Agricultural Plant Varieties of the People's Republic of China", used to prove: 1. To date, the Ministry of Agriculture has not accepted any application concerning tea tree variety rights, and "Taoyuan Daye" has not been granted variety rights; 2. Appellee Gudongchun Company does not hold variety rights for "Taoyuan Daye".

**Set Three:** A letter of commitment and a public notice, used to prove that "Taoyuan Daye Tea" is a product subject to protection of origin; with the consent of the Taoyuan County Government, Appellant Yiqingyuan Company has the right to invest in the development, production, processing, and promotion of the "Taoyuan Daye" tea variety.

**Set Four:** Photographs, certificates, and agreements for processing "Taoyuan Daye Tea", used to prove: 1. Appellant Yiqingyuan Company is a member enterprise of the Taohuayuan Tea Group; 2. Yiqingyuan Company has a 12,000-mu tea production base in Taoyuan County; 3. Yiqingyuan Company only processes and purchases tea products (i.e., sells agricultural by-products) produced by tea farmers within Taoyuan County, and does not directly produce or sell tea tree varieties (i.e., does not deal in seedlings); 4. The "Yezhenwang", "Yezhen Maojian", and "Yezhen Green Tea" produced by Yiqingyuan Company indeed originate from within Taoyuan County.

**Set Five:** "Business License for Enterprise Legal Person", "Capital Verification Report", actual tea packaging and photographs, used to prove: 1. Appellant Yiqingyuan Company was established earlier, while Appellee Gudongchun Company was established later; Gudongchun Company cannot prove prior use of "Yechawang"; 2. "Yechawang" is a generic name for tea, not an "original" product name of Gudongchun Company; 3. The differences between Yiqingyuan's "Yezhenwang" and Gudongchun's "Yechawang" products are obvious and would not cause consumer confusion.

**Set Six:** Certificates of honor, awards, and news reports, used to prove that the Yiqingyuan series of tea is indeed a well-known product.

Appellee Gudongchun Company orally argued in defense: "Yechawang" and "Yecha" are well-known products and are the exclusive product names of the appellee. The actions of Appellant Yiqingyuan Company and the defendants at first instance, including Zhang Guohua, constitute infringement and they shall bear corresponding liability according to law. The original judgment was fair and reasonable, and the legal characterization was correct. The appellee requested that the first-instance judgment be affirmed.

Appellee Gudongchun Company additionally submitted one piece of evidence, i.e., a promotional report from *Hunan Daily*, used to prove the continuing infringement by Appellant Yiqingyuan Company.

Upon further investigation, the Hunan High People's Court found the following facts: On July 25, 1996, Appellant Yiqingyuan Company was established. Through cooperation with local governments and farmers, the company established a tea production base in Taoyuan County, selecting, breeding, and procuring "Taoyuan Daye" raw materials. The products it produced and sold included Yiqingyuan "Yezhenwang", "Yechawang", "Yezhen Green Tea", "Yezhen Maojian", and "Yecha Maojian". The registered trademark "Yiqingyuan" was awarded the title "Hunan Province Famous Trademark". The Yiqingyuan series of tea products was awarded the title of famous brand product by the Hunan Province Famous Brand Evaluation Committee. Yiqingyuan "Yezhenwang" tea won the gold award in the tea evaluation of the Shanghai International Cultural Festival and China Premium Famous Tea Expo, as well as numerous other provincial and national awards. Yiqingyuan Company was recognized as a leading enterprise in agricultural industrialization in Hunan Province and enjoys high recognition within the industry. The tea shops operated by the defendants at first instance, Zhang Guohua and Zhang Zhi, as well as the defendants at first instance, Jiayongduo Changde Store, Jiayongduo Chenzhou Store, Tongcheng Kongtai Dongtang Store, Huayin Wanghe Xinzhong Road Store, Huayin Wanghe Dongfeng Company, Huayin Wanghe Jiefang Road Store, and Xinlianxin Supermarket Liangmao Store, all sold tea products such as "Yezhen Maojian", "Yecha Maojian", "Yezhen Green Tea", "Yezhenwang", and "Yechawang" produced by Yiqingyuan Company. On November 8, 1996, the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station was cancelled upon approval. The Rural Work Office of the People's Government of Taoyuan County agreed that "the original enterprise personnel would form shareholders and continue to engage in tea plant research. The original factory premises, equipment, and its debts would be assumed by the new company." However, it did not specify whether the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station had any intangible assets or how they should be handled, nor was this reflected in the "Enterprise Application for Cancellation of Registration Form". On November 11, 1996, Lu Wanjun, Lu Honggao, Lu Liqun, Tang Chunxian, and Lu Shaoping, as shareholders, jointly invested to establish Appellee Gudongchun Company. Using "Taoyuan Daye" as raw material, the company produced and sold Gudongchun (registered trademark) "Yechawang", "Yecha", and other tea products. It was further found that within Taoyuan County, other tea products were also produced and sold, such as Taohuayuan brand "Yechawang", Lingya brand "Yechawang", and Xianglong brand "Yecha". On October 19, 2004, the Taoyuan County Government applied for protection of "Taoyuan Daye" tea as a product of geographical origin, which was accepted by the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine upon formal examination and was publicly announced. Apart from the above, as the parties had no dispute over other facts determined by the first and second instances, the second instance confirmed them.

The issues in dispute in this case were: 1. Whether Appellee Gudongchun Company enjoyed the right of discovery of the wild maternal tea plant "Taoyuan Daye" and whether it had obtained the variety right for the "Taoyuan Daye" tea tree. 2. Whether Appellant Yiqingyuan Company had engaged in the act of using, without authorization, the unique name of another's well-known product or a name similar thereto, causing confusion with another's well-known product and leading purchasers to mistake it; whether it had engaged in the act of using advertisements or other means to make false representations about the quality of its goods; and whether it had engaged in the act of fabricating and disseminating false facts to damage the business reputation or product reputation of a competitor.

The Hunan High People's Court held:

**Regarding the first issue.** The right of discovery and the variety right are two distinct concepts. Article 97 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law* provides: "Citizens shall have the right of discovery with respect to their discoveries. The discoverer has the right to apply for and receive discovery certificates, bonuses, or other awards." This provision clarifies that the right of discovery is merely a right to honor and a right to be rewarded enjoyed by the discoverer. The object of the right of discovery is pre-existing natural facts, and the discoverer does not have an exclusive right to control the object of their discovery. Moreover, discovery itself is also a fact, so the right of discovery cannot be transferred, licensed for others' use, or acquired by succession. The discoverer may enjoy spiritual benefits, such as obtaining certificates, indicating status, receiving honors, etc., and may also obtain bonuses or other rewards. Based on the facts established in this case, the right of discovery of the wild maternal tea plant "Taoyuan Daye" should be enjoyed by the local masses who discovered this wild tea plant and by the employees of the former Taoyuan County Taopupu Tea Farm, Lu Wanjun, Huang Hanyuan, et al. Appellee Gudongchun Company does not enjoy the right of discovery of the wild maternal tea plant "Taoyuan Daye".

Article 2 of the *Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties* provides: "'New plant varieties' as mentioned in these Regulations refer to plant varieties that have been artificially cultivated or developed from discovered wild plants, possessing novelty, distinctness, uniformity, and stability, and which have been appropriately named." Article 3 of these Regulations provides: "The administrative departments of agriculture and forestry of the State Council (hereinafter collectively referred to as the 'approval authorities') shall, according to their respective functions and duties, be jointly responsible for the reception and examination of applications for new plant variety rights and shall grant new plant variety rights (hereinafter 'variety rights') to new plant varieties that meet the requirements of these Regulations." Article 31 of these Regulations provides: "For an application for variety rights that meets the requirements of these Regulations after substantive examination, the approval authority shall make a decision to grant the variety right, issue a variety right certificate, and make a registration and announcement." According to the above provisions, obtaining a plant variety right requires submitting an application for variety rights to the Ministry of Agriculture or the Ministry of Forestry, which shall conduct substantive examination of the application according to statutory procedures, and for those that meet the relevant requirements after examination, decide to grant the variety right, issue a variety right certificate to the applicant, and at the same time make a registration and announcement. Without going through the above procedures, no individual or entity can originally obtain a variety right by any other means. The new tea tree variety "Taoyuan Daye" is a new tea tree variety formed by the Research Institute of the Agricultural College and the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station through the selection and breeding of the wild large-leaf tea tree. The new tea tree variety "Taoyuan Daye" could not have arisen through "discovery", nor does there exist a so-called "right of discovery" for a new tea tree variety. In this case, although the "Taoyuan Daye" tea tree variety objectively exists, it was not granted variety rights by the approval authority according to statutory procedures. The original trial court's finding that Appellee Gudongchun Company enjoyed variety rights for "Taoyuan Daye" was erroneous.

Furthermore, the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station was legally cancelled, while Appellee Gudongchun Company is a limited liability company established by contributions from natural persons including Lu Wanjun. There is no legal succession relationship between the two entities. Looking at the process of the cancellation of the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station and the establishment of Gudongchun Company, although there was an opinion from the Rural Work Office of the People's Government of Taoyuan County agreeing that "the original enterprise personnel would form shareholders and continue to engage in tea plant research. The original factory premises, equipment, and its debts would be assumed by the new company", there is no evidence proving that the intangible assets of the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station were handled at that time, let alone the fact that intangible assets were transferred to Gudongchun Company. Moreover, the Taoyuan Tea Seed Station did not enjoy variety rights for "Taoyuan Daye". In summary, Gudongchun Company neither enjoys the right of discovery of the wild maternal tea plant "Taoyuan Daye" nor the variety right for the "Taoyuan Daye" tea tree. The relevant grounds of appeal of Appellant Yiqingyuan Company are sustainable.

**Regarding the second issue.** According to China's *Anti-Unfair Competition Law* and the *Several Provisions of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on Prohibiting Unfair Competition Acts of Counterfeiting the Unique Names, Packaging, and Decoration of Well-Known Products*, a well-known product refers to a product that has a certain degree of market reputation and is known to the relevant public. A unique name of a well-known product refers to a product name that is exclusive to that well-known product and is significantly different from generic names.

Determining whether a specific product is a well-known product should be done by comprehensively considering factors such as the product's history of production and sale in a specific market, sales territory, sales volume, market share, reputation, and advertising investment and coverage. In this case, although Appellee Gudongchun Company claimed that its "Yechawang" and "Yecha" series of products were well-known, it neither provided evidence regarding the time, territory, and volume of their production and sale, the timing of advertising and promotion, nor the evaluations of relevant consumer groups, nor did it provide evidence such as award certificates or media reports for its products. The evidence submitted by Gudongchun Company regarding the awards for "Taoyuan Daye" tea can only prove the history of the emergence, development, and recognition of "Taoyuan Daye", but cannot lead to the conclusion that the series of products produced and sold by Gudongchun Company are well-known products.

Determining whether a product name is the unique name of a well-known product first requires establishing that a certain business operator used it earlier. In this case, Appellee Gudongchun Company was established after Appellant Yiqingyuan Company. Gudongchun Company only submitted to the court its tea packaging boxes marked with "Yechawang" and "Yecha", but the production time of these products could not be determined. Combined with the fact that within Taoyuan County, tea products like Taohuayuan brand "Yechawang" and Lingya brand "Yechawang" were also produced and sold, this indicates that the names "Yechawang" and "Yecha" have been commonly used by multiple enterprises and are generic to the related products. Furthermore, the unique name of a well-known product must possess distinct character, enabling it to be distinguished from other related products. In this case, "Yechawang" and "Yecha" are merely descriptive of the composition of the product and, when used alone, do not indicate the source of the product. Therefore, what distinguishes the products of the two parties are the registered trademarks "Yiqingyuan" and "Gudongchun", not "Yechawang" or "Yecha". Moreover, the packaging and decoration of Yiqingyuan Company's products are clearly different from those of Gudongchun Company's products, which would not cause confusion among the relevant public. Furthermore, as stated above, the "Yechawang" series of products produced and sold by Gudongchun Company cannot be recognized as well-known products. In summary, it cannot be determined that "Yechawang" and "Yecha" are the unique product names of Gudongchun Company's tea products. The grounds of appeal of Yiqingyuan Company, that its production and sale of "Yechawang" and "Yezhenwang" tea products do not constitute an infringement of Gudongchun Company's product name right and do not constitute unfair competition, are sustainable.

Article 5, paragraph (4) of the *Anti-Unfair Competition Law* provides that business operators shall not engage in market transactions by using unfair means such as forging or fraudulently using quality marks like certification marks or prestigious brand marks, forging the place of origin, or making misleading false representations as to the quality of goods, thereby harming competitors. Article 9 of that Law provides that business operators shall not use advertisements or other methods to make misleading or false representations concerning the quality, composition, performance, use, producer, validity period, or place of origin of their goods. Appellant Yiqingyuan Company provided the court with substantial evidence that it had established tea production and processing bases in Taoyuan County and had procured raw materials for "Taoyuan Daye" tea, proving that it not only built its own tea base in Taoyuan County through cooperation with local governments and farmers, selecting and breeding high-quality tea tree varieties, but also signed agreements with tea companies, tea processing plants, and tea farmers within Taoyuan County for the procurement and processing of tea products, thereby purchasing large quantities of "Taoyuan Daye" tea as raw materials to produce and process the Yiqingyuan brand series of tea products. Although Appellee Gudongchun Company raised objections, it did not provide sufficient evidence to prove that Yiqingyuan Company's relevant evidence was untruthful. Therefore, the grounds of appeal of Yiqingyuan Company that it did not forge the place of origin of its tea products and did not make false representations about the composition of its products are sustainable.

Both Appellant Yiqingyuan Company and Appellee Gudongchun Company produce, process, and sell tea products using "Taoyuan Daye" as the raw material. The higher the recognition of "Taoyuan Daye", the more beneficial it is for the tea production and sales of related enterprises. By compiling the book *Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* and promoting/introducing "Taoyuan Daye" on its company website and product packaging, Yiqingyuan Company raised the profile of "Taoyuan Daye". This action not only failed to disparage competitors or damage the business reputation or product reputation of Gudongchun Company, but actually benefited all tea production enterprises (including Gudongchun Company) that use "Taoyuan Daye" as a raw material, helping them enhance market recognition and market share. Although some content in *Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* regarding the discovery, selection and breeding, naming, identification, and examination of the wild maternal tea plant and the "Taoyuan Daye" tea tree variety might be inconsistent with objective facts, since Gudongchun Company neither enjoys the right of discovery of the wild "Taoyuan Daye" tea plant nor the variety right for "Taoyuan Daye", Gudongchun Company is not the infringed party even if such inaccuracies exist in the book. Therefore, whether the relevant descriptions in *Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* contain inaccuracies is not within the scope of the trial of this case.

In summary, the facts found by the first instance were unclear, and the law was incorrectly applied. The production and sale of Yiqingyuan "Yechawang", "Yezhenwang", "Yezhen Green Tea", "Yecha Maojian" and other tea products by Appellant Yiqingyuan Company and the defendants at first instance, and Yiqingyuan Company's promotion of "Taoyuan Daye" and its own products through *Introduction to Tea and Tea Culture* and its company website, do not constitute unfair competition against Appellee Gudongchun Company. The grounds of appeal of Yiqingyuan Company are sustainable.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 5(2) and (4), Article 9(1), and Article 14 of the *Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China*, and Article 153(2) and (3) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, the Hunan High People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 23, 2004:

**I.** The civil judgment (2004) Chang Min San Chu Zi No. 9 of the Changde Intermediate People's Court is reversed;

**II.** The claims of Gudongchun Company are dismissed.
